events.text: A temple keeper bars the shrine door while you are still kneeling in the hall of small offerings. {He} sets out two bowls of steeped bitter leaf, the kind worshippers leave at dusk, and waits for the steam to fall. "You were angry when the prayers came in," {he} says. "Gods are, a little. But there is a place to put it."

choices.text: Stay and learn to pour

effects.log: {npc} corrects your wrist nine times. By the tenth bowl you have forgotten which prayer angered you. (Rite of the Steeped Offering begun.)

choices.text: Thank {him} for the bowl and go

effects.log: Good leaf. {npc} nods as if that were also an answer.

events.text: A steward of the divine exchange reads your tally of offerings over your shoulder and sighs. "Three entries, and all three favour the shrine." {He} draws a knotted tally-cord from {his} sleeve as a priest draws an amulet. "Sit. Faith is the only thing that compounds while a god sleeps."

choices.text: Learn the steward's method

effects.log: By nightfall you have found the three entries and two more nobody mentioned. (Tithe-Reckoning begun.)

choices.text: Say tithes are not your domain

effects.log: "They are everyone's domain," {npc} says, and goes back to the exchange to wait for the next one.

events.text: A warden of the totem groves, one ear notched by an old tusk, is binding a wounded fox-spirit at a shrine gate and says without looking up that a boar-saint trailed you from the last offering. "It let you pass. Do you know why?" {He} points to ash-marks on the ground that you never noticed.

choices.text: Kneel and learn to read them

effects.log: {npc} walks you through a year of spoor in one afternoon, and gives you a vial for your trouble. (Lore of the Totem Beasts begun.)

choices.text: Thank {him} and take the longer path

effects.log: You take the longer path. You sleep very well.

events.text: An old tithe-gardener pulls a bloom out of your hand before you finish picking it. "That one is for the dead, and it angers the living," {he} says, and reads the whole first-fruit field once, the way a scribe reads a vow. "Offerings that take root grow leeward. Nobody told you. Come."

choices.text: Follow {him} down the rows

effects.log: You come away with a basket, and a field you will never see the same way again. (First-Fruit Reading begun.)

choices.text: Keep your own basket

effects.log: You pick where you were picking. You leave out the one for the dead.

events.text: An ascetic has knelt at a roadside shrine since your first blessing, and moss has taken the hem of {his} robe. When you pass at dusk {his} eyes open. "Your power leaks," {he} says, like noting a roof. "Each failed ascent, you pour out an age. Why do you do that?"

choices.text: Ask {him} how not to

effects.log: One breath a day for a month, then fewer. You had not known how much of you was hurrying. (Breath of the Patient Shell begun.)

choices.text: Leave a coin of faith in the bowl and go on

effects.log: The eyes close again. The moss has not noticed you were there.

events.text: A pilgrim lies crushed under a toppled votive pillar, and a healer-priest kneels beside the stone and looks up at you. "You. Strong arms. Hold the knee and watch my hands, because I am ancient and no temple on this road has ever watched."

choices.text: Hold the knee, and watch

effects.log: There is one soft sound, and the groaning stops. {npc} shows you the trick again on a chicken bone over supper. (Mending Hands of the Hall begun.)

choices.text: Hold the knee, and leave when it is done

effects.log: It is done quickly. You do not ask how, and you are not sure you wanted to know.

events.text: A shepherd-god's attendant snaps a woven cord at a gnat on your shoulder: the gnat is gone, the cloth is not. {He} lifts a coin off a pilgrim child's brow the same way and returns it. "A soft cord goes around," {he} says. "Everyone wants the crack. You watched the wrist."

choices.text: Ask about the wrist

effects.log: Three weeks in the shepherd's fold and a welt on every part of you, and one dawn the cord does what you meant. (Shepherd's Cord begun.)

choices.text: Bow and move on

effects.log: A coin thrown by a pilgrim beside you never lands. It reaches {his} hand, by the cord.

events.text: A fallen scribe of the Book of Fates duels a drunk demigod outside a wine-hall, using a blade like a copyist's pen. Three strokes, and the demigod's sash reads "fool" in a fine hand. {npc} sees you staring. "You write as well," {he} says. "Most who can are ashamed of one."

choices.text: Say you are ashamed of neither

effects.log: {npc} laughs until {he} coughs, then writes you a page of strokes with the blade, on an altar-step. It takes you a year to read. (Scribe's Blade begun.)

choices.text: Fetch {him} the next jar instead

effects.log: A good evening. By its end {he} has insulted every god you know, accurately.

events.text: A blind hymn-singer stops mid-psalm to say that a novice three altars over has lit the wrong lamp. The hall laughs. Ten breaths later a startled voice calls out about a lamp. Afterwards {he} finds you. "You turned your head. Shall I show you how a prayer is heard before it is spoken?"

choices.text: Yes, and kneel with your eyes shut

effects.log: A season in a dark chapel beside a stranger's breathing. Then one night you know who is climbing the steps. (Prayer-Hearing begun.)

choices.text: Ask only what the lamp was for

effects.log: "A rite for the Book," says {npc}. You change chapels.

events.text: You leave a coin at a roadside shrine on Monday. On Tuesday a young attendant stops you and asks after your offering in your own voice. {npc} laughs at your face. "Nobody looks at a face where gods walk. They look at your halo, and a halo is only a posture. I have watched you. You could wear many."

choices.text: Learn the borrowed halo

effects.log: For a month you are a porter, then a pilgrim, then nobody. Your oldest worshipper would pass you at a shrine gate. (Many Avatars begun.)

choices.text: Decline, and watch your sleeve

effects.log: Your sleeve is as you left it. A votive coin has been slipped inside.

events.text: An old standard-bearer of a lost pantheon war keeps the host's banners in a cedar chest and lays them among the offering-bowls. "This is the pass," {he} says. "You hold a hundred godlings, and a storm. Tell me what you do, and I will tell you when they fall."

choices.text: Move an offering-bowl

effects.log: Your hundred are lost six times before the incense burns down. On the seventh {npc} studies the bowls without speaking. (Standard of the Host begun.)

choices.text: Say the war is long over

effects.log: "It is," {npc} says, and puts away the banners one at a time, in the order they fell.

events.text: At a funeral rite for a worshipper no god remembered, an old mourner hums beneath the choir, a line that makes your teeth feel far away. {He} stops when {he} sees you listening. "Your ear is not for the living," {he} says, kindly. "Most gods would have felt nothing."

choices.text: Ask {him} to teach you the line

effects.log: It has no words. It has an order in which you stop being afraid of things. You learn the first of them that winter. (Psalm of the Soul begun.)

choices.text: Pay your respects and leave

effects.log: You leave a lamp for the unremembered. The line follows you down the temple steps and then lets you go.

events.text: A hermit-demigod on a bare altar-rock watches you run your rite and winces as if bitten. "That rite and your domain are quarrelling. You will win, and it will cost your whole age. One element feeds the next. Do you know what that means, or do you only recite it?"

choices.text: Admit you only recite it

effects.log: You turn in a circle for a hundred days, wood to fire to earth, until your domain stops arguing. (Fivefold Domain Turning begun.)

choices.text: Say your rite has served you well

effects.log: "It has," says {npc}. "Ask it what it charged."

events.text: In a school for acolytes the slowest novice in three temples has been given the same sum since the first-fruit feast. You watch the catechist try a ninth way, and a tenth. On the eleventh the novice looks up. {npc} sees you see it. "Anyone can do it once," {he} says. "Will you learn to do it again?"

choices.text: Take the bench beside {him} for a season

effects.log: You are very bad at it. Then one afternoon somebody's novice understands, and you have to step outside. (Catechist's Art begun.)

choices.text: Leave a gift for the school

effects.log: The novice carries it to the catechist with both hands, and has counted it correctly.

events.text: On the pilgrim stair to a mountain shrine a tiny old bearer passes you with a censer on {his} back, descends, and passes you again. "You stop to breathe," {he} says on the third pass. "That is why you must stop. Will you carry something?"

choices.text: Take a censer

effects.log: You carry censers for a month and learn to climb the way water comes down. (Pilgrim's Stair Breath begun.)

choices.text: Sit on the step and tell {him} to go on

effects.log: You sit. The view of the valley shrines is very fine. {npc} passes twice more before you rise.

events.text: A rival god of the next domain has come to your shrine to unseat you, and is drinking your steeped leaf. You both know. You pour again, slowly, and watch the tremor leave {his} hand before it leaves yours. Meditation now begins at the fifth breath. You wonder if {he} can tell.

choices.text: Ask {him} who sent {him}, between cups

effects.log: {npc} tells you on the third cup and asks for a fourth. By morning the border has one fewer quarrel, and no worshipper was harmed.

choices.text: Say nothing, and see {him} to the shrine gate

effects.log: The tale crosses three domains. Worshippers begin to arrive at your gate who bring no offering but a question.

events.text: A temple ox bolts through the festival market with a child on its yoke. Your cord is round its horns before you decide anything, and then you hold an ox. Afterwards {npc}, keeper of the sacred herds, wipes {his} hands. "You never hurt its mouth. I have a beast nobody can touch. It wants a hand like that."

choices.text: Go and look at the beast

effects.log: It bites you, then stops. You leave with a vial of its essence, freely given, and an offer of work. What you best on the road may now follow you home.

choices.text: Return the child and go

effects.log: The mother cannot speak. The ox tries to follow you for a while.

events.text: Your own rite has stood still for an age, and you copy an old hymn to rest. Halfway down the page you notice that the third stroke is the rite. You stop and look at your hand. A collector of the Celestial Ministries stands in the door with a ledger and has seen your face. "Shall I come back?" {he} says.

choices.text: Ask {him} to come back

effects.log: You write until the lamp dies. Your own art comes easier now, as anything does that has been written once.

choices.text: Settle the account, then return to the page

effects.log: It does not go away. It waits, as a good verse does.

events.text: You share a ferry with two hunters of the Celestial Ministries who carry your likeness on a slip. One reads it aloud. "Tall, left-handed, walks as if owed worship." You are a stout incense-seller with a cough, asking {npc} about the price of myrrh. Their eyes slide over you like water.

choices.text: Offer them some incense

effects.log: One of them buys a stick from you. It is the most frightening thing you have done this age. They go on searching, farther away.

choices.text: Step off at the next landing

effects.log: You step off. A century later you hear they are still riding that route.

events.text: At a muster of a lesser pantheon's temple-guard you are asked, as a courtesy, to look over the line. You move four spears and a standard. {npc}, their captain, stares at the field a long while and sends for an old map. "A pantheon could be beaten from here," {he} says. "If anyone ever wished it."

choices.text: Draw {him} the map

effects.log: Your name begins to turn up where a god's name does not. In any war your faction joins, the host will stand where you tell it.

choices.text: Tell {him} to burn the map

effects.log: {npc} burns it. You watch the smoke, then draw it again, for yourself, from memory.

events.text: You are humming in a sickroom for nobody in particular, and the dying worshipper sits up to say that {npc} is at the door. {npc} is. "It is your humming," the worshipper says. "It goes further than you do." You feel it then, the part of you that lives past the temple walls.

choices.text: Keep humming, and follow it

effects.log: You sit up with it until dawn. Your soul sits a little farther out in you than it did yesterday.

choices.text: Stop, and see who is at the door

effects.log: {npc} has brought soup. You are grateful for a door with only somebody at it.

events.text: An acolyte you gave up on returns after a century with a domain-seal at the belt. {npc} bows to you on the temple steps before everyone, then repeats something you once said that you do not recall saying. {He} has built a whole office on it.

choices.text: Pretend you remember

effects.log: You nod slowly, and {npc} is delighted. You spend the evening afraid of the things you might have said.

choices.text: Admit you do not remember

effects.log: {npc} laughs for a long time. "That is the best thing you ever taught me." You will be asked to teach again.

events.text: A steward of your shrine brings the year's tithe-rolls with a pleasant smile. You read them as you would a stance, and on the eleventh scroll find the one figure standing badly. {npc} watches your finger stop. {He} has stopped smiling, and is working out what you know.

choices.text: Say nothing, and have the figure corrected

effects.log: The missing offerings turn up next month with a note about a clerk. Your rolls have not been wrong since.

choices.text: Ask {him} about it before the staff

effects.log: {npc} leaves the shrine. Every clerk you keep now sits a little straighter.

events.text: On a landing of the pilgrim stair where you once knelt a whole season gasping, you find you have climbed still breathing as on level ground. {npc}, a pilgrim slumped against the rail with a staff across the knees, looks up. "Are you even tired?"

choices.text: Sit and show {him} the breath

effects.log: You sit with {npc} for an hour. The stair does not seem to mind. Neither of you is anyone in particular, for that hour.

choices.text: Say "Not yet," and go on up

effects.log: You go on. Your breath is the only sound on the stair, and it does not change.

events.text: You taste the ash for days. Then a stranger stops you on a temple causeway, calls you by a name you never had, and asks if you have finally paid. {He} does not seem surprised at your silence. "It is a start," says {npc}, and walks on. You have three years less and feel lighter.

choices.text: Go after {him} and ask the name

effects.log: {npc} tells you. It means nothing. In the night you remember what it means.

choices.text: Let {him} go, and light lamps at the next shrine

effects.log: You light a lamp at the next shrine, and one at the one after. It becomes a habit you did not ask for.

choices.text: Let {him} go

effects.log: You watch {him} cross. The lightness stays a little longer than you expected.

events.text: You are at a pilgrim inn far from any shrine that knows you when someone in the next room tells {npc} how you were sealed away, and how you died. The telling is good. The teller was at the seal. You hear the cold of you, and the bell, and sit with your rice through the part where the warden wept.

choices.text: Stay dead for a while

effects.log: It is restful. Nobody prays to the dead.

choices.text: Send the teller a jug

effects.log: The teller stares at you a long time and accepts it. The story is better the next night.

events.text: The sickness of the Cup of Emptying lasts a month. When you can stand, you test yourself with a lesser pill, and it takes as it did in your youth. {npc}, a keeper of the pharmacopoeia, studies your tongue and your eyes. "You will not find that twice," {he} says. "Spend it on something."

choices.text: Ask what {he} would spend it on

effects.log: {npc} tells you. It is not what you expected, and it is not a pill.

choices.text: Ask for the keeper's best on loan against a favour

effects.log: It is good, and you feel it land.

choices.text: Thank {him} and rest another week

effects.log: The week passes in a quiet cell. You are strangely content.

events.text: The Seed of Another Soil has done its work, and your old rite runs without its old quarrel. Then a god of your nature's own element meets you on a causeway and stops dead. "What have you done?" says {npc}, staring at something you cannot see. "It leans. Your nature leans. Who did that to you?"

choices.text: Say you did it yourself

effects.log: {npc} looks at you as at an interesting ruin. {He} writes it down.

choices.text: Ask whether it can be read

effects.log: {npc} reads it, on the causeway, two fingers at your wrist. {He} never stops frowning, and never stops reading.

events.text: Evening at a wayside inn the pilgrim-roads pass through. The travellers have brought out the thin wine, and {npc} is telling the one about the goat for the fifth time this season. You laugh in the right place. You did not have to remember to. Far below you, something sealed turns over in its sleep.

choices.text: Tell the goat story yourself next time

effects.log: You tell it badly. It becomes your story anyway. They begin to call it yours.

choices.text: Go to your room early and sit with it

effects.log: You sit. It is quiet. You are, you notice, not unhappy, and you leave that alone.

events.text: A catechist comes to your door with a slate. {He} has taught the young one of your house for a season and has now been corrected, on a point held for thirty years, by a child eating a fig. "I do not know what you did," says {npc}. "I would like to know what you intend to do about it."

choices.text: Summon finer teachers from the great temples

effects.log: They come, and one by one they leave, somewhat quieter. The child does not notice them go.

choices.text: Ask {him} to stay and be corrected

effects.log: {npc} stays, and it is the happiest {he} has been in years. The two argue at breakfast.

events.text: Your neighbour {npc} stops you at the shrine well and asks what you did. The old one in your house was up on the roof this morning, mending it, shouting down about a debt from twenty years ago. "We were all so sure," {he} says. {He} does not sound entirely pleased. "Is there any more of it?"

choices.text: Send over a bowl of plain broth

effects.log: It is only broth. {npc} is better within the week, and tells everyone.

choices.text: Say it will not work on those who ask

effects.log: {npc} laughs and almost believes you. You go up and help with the roof.

events.text: They say you can see it on those who tried an ascent on a firebrand vow. {npc}, an old gatekeeper of some forgotten shrine, sees it on you across a courtyard. {He} points to {his} own throat, where the scar runs down. "Once," {he} says. "We all think once. Did it open?"

choices.text: Say what happened

effects.log: {npc} hears all of it, then tells you {his} own, which is much worse, and asks you to stop there.

choices.text: Ask who sells the embers

effects.log: {npc} tells you, and looks away first.
